newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel price holds up, despite crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel price holds up, despite crude.

text.p: Straight-run prices in northern Europe were steady on Wednesday after their sharp fall the day before, though weak crude suggested prices problems ahead, traders said.
The market for low sulphur straight-run was quiet, with traders still pondering the $89.50 fob heard paid for an Irish cargo on Tuesday.
Despite that price sellers said offers were holding steady at $93 fob or above, though no deals were done.
Russian cargoes were appearing with expected regularity for the season, traders said.
One British major was heard to have picked up an M-100 to add to two other straight-run cargoes purchased earlier in the week.

In the Mediterranean the St. Nicholas 2, with high sulphur M100 was heard still available, and at least two low sulphur M100s were believed on offer, with demand reported moderate to weak. - London newsroom +44 171 542 8060
